target_customer: Skip hire and waste collection operators running short-haul truck fleets
problem: Dispatchers plan routes manually and lose margin on mismatched trucks and jobs, especially when jobs and drivers change during the day.
business_model: B2B SaaS scheduling agent integrated with existing ERPs, pricing not found
product_category: AI scheduling and dispatch for waste logistics

founders.name: George Postlethwaite
founders.background_notes: YC page says he and co-founder met at Oxford; education not listed.

competitors.name: Waste Logics
competitors.what: Skip hire and trade waste software with drag-and-drop scheduling and route optimisation

competitors.name: Access Weighsoft
competitors.what: Multi-industry waste ERP that Dayjob integrates with

competitors.name: Routeware
competitors.what: Cloud skip hire platform with optimisation engine

technical_complexity.rationale: Vehicle routing with live re-planning and ERP integrations is standard operations research engineering with hard integration parts.

defensibility.rationale: Deep ERP integration and operator workflows create stickiness, but ERP vendors and routing vendors could add similar AI features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early to know; one review found none of five skip hire vendors advertised skip-specific AI.

market_need_then: Operators claim margin loss from poor scheduling; Dayjob's site claims 11% revenue gain and 25% less admin time, which are unverified company claims.

branding.domain_note: Original site getdayjob.ai now redirects to dayjob.ai (seen 2026).

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and benefit-led, aimed at operators, 'AI technology, backed by real people'

brand_strength.rationale: Plain, memorable word but generic (a design agency also uses Day Job) and no press on the brand.

outcome_analysis: Dayjob is early, targeting UK skip hire operators and expanding to the US per a YC launch page. Founders previously built an ERP for e-waste recyclers, a plausible domain edge. No outcome events were found and funding is unconfirmed, so the outcome is unknown.
notes: Aggregators disagree on funding and none is confirmed by a primary source: Standout $1.6M pre-seed, Neuronfeed $500K seed in January 2026, Welcome to the Jungle $0.7M (Dec 2024) plus $0.4M angel (Jul 2023), Simplify $130K for Dayjobai, Inc. No rounds recorded. YC page cites a VWS partnership (30 Jan 2026) and a Coastal Recycling case study (27 Jan 2026), which could not be independently confirmed. Founder education other than Fooks not found.
